citation: "Kinzie Mansion—1812." — halftone plate after Sarony's lithograph, in Joseph Kirkland, The Chicago Massacre of 1812 (Chicago: Dibble Publishing Co., 1893), p. 73.
author: after Napoleon Sarony's lithograph of a sketch by Juliette A. Kinzie; the 1893 plate's maker is not named
repository: Project Gutenberg eBook #59624 (images/page73.png); the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_kinzie_mansion_1812_kirkland_1893.png (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md); the volume is also Internet Archive chicagomass00kirkrich (chicago/reference/chicago-massacre-1812.yaml)
locator: p. 73, the plate captioned 'KINZIE MANSION—1812.', 600 x 353 px as Project Gutenberg serves it
rights_note: Published 1893 in the United States, out of copyright by age.
access_notes: Fetched from Project Gutenberg and read off the image itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2498); the page and caption are read from the Gutenberg text's page markers.
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof along the river, the east end toward the eye's right, a piazza across the front on posts with a rail
a picket fence round the green before the house down toward the water, a landing at the water's edge
four columnar Lombardy poplars in a row east of the house running toward the river, and a great broad-crowned tree behind it
two stacks through the ridge, and outbuildings and a two-storey house up the road to the west, behind the house
what_it_does_not_supply: anything the Currey plate does not: it is the same artwork, cropped a little closer, and its 1812 caption is Kirkland's reading of it, not the artist's
note: Kept as its own record because it is a separate publication with its own date claim (1812); for the house's form it is a copy of sarony_kinzie_residence_currey_1912_plate and adds no evidence.
